requirement_text.REQ-421:
Build-order M2, MOB-2 in docs/mobile/requirements.md. The gate for the whole tier: after this, a build can log into a tenant. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (authentication flow, token handling).
SEQUENCE: 1. Tenant identity from manual slug entry or a deep link (https://<slug>.<platform-host>/..., Android intent filter for https with host *.<platform-host>, where <platform-host> is supplied at build time from the same build configuration as LETFLOW_API_BASE_URL -- e.g. a --dart-define plus a Gradle manifestPlaceholder -- never a tenant slug; iOS universal-link entitlement written but DEFERRED -- no iOS build on this host). Verified App Link status (android:autoVerify) needs /.well-known/assetlinks.json served by the platform host, which no requirement provides: declare the filter without relying on verification and record verification as DEFERRED with that reason. The slug is the only tenant input; nothing tenant specific is compiled in (REQ-419's guard stays green). 2. GET {LETFLOW_API_BASE_URL}/api/mobile/tenant-config?slug=<slug> with NO Authorization header. Consume realm_url, client_id (added by REQ-418), locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind. The endpoint never errors on an unknown slug: by its anti-enumeration never-error rule it returns platform defaults, including realm_url for the default realm "bpm-default" (@default_realm, lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex:151,199). The app therefore CANNOT detect an unknown slug before login, and must not try to (that would be the enumeration oracle the endpoint refuses to be). "Tenant not found" is detected AFTER login instead: the FIRST entry of GET /api/v1/me/memberships is always the tenant the token itself serves (lib/letflow/routers/me.ex moduledoc, "Response shape": the handler prepends the caller's own current tenant); every later entry is a tenant the subject could switch into by re-authenticating, and the backend scopes every request to the token's tenant, not to the slug the user typed. So: if the first entry's tenant_slug does not equal the entered slug, show tenant-not-found and delete the just-stored tokens -- even when a later entry matches (matching any entry would let the app label tenant A's data as tenant B's; v1 does not perform the re-authentication a switch needs). CANDIDATE users get 403 from /me/memberships by design (lib/letflow/routers/me.ex, "MembershipsRead -- CANDIDATE deliberately excluded"); on that 403 skip the membership check and rely on /me/modules. Document this rule in code comments. 3. flutter_appauth authorizeAndExchangeCode with issuer = realm_url, clientId = client_id from step 2 (never a compiled constant), redirectUrl com.bizdala.letflow:/oauth2redirect, PKCE S256 (flutter_appauth default). Android: Custom Tabs via the appAuthRedirectScheme manifest placeholder; no webview anywhere (REQ-419's dependency guard forbids webview packages). 4. Tokens persisted ONLY through one class in lib/auth/ backed by flutter_secure_storage, keyed by tenant (realm_url) so tenant A's tokens are never presented to tenant B. REQ-422 hardens and guards this; REQ-421 must not introduce any other storage path for tokens. 5. Before any tenant content: GET /api/v1/me/memberships and GET /api/v1/me/modules (lib/letflow/routers/me.ex:74, :78) and build the route table from installed_modules (architecture.md §6 -- a module not installed has no route at all). 6. Four dedicated error screens: tenant-not-found, network-unavailable, OIDC-failure, secure-storage-unavailable. 7. Create lib/api/api_client.dart as the ONLY place a Dio instance is constructed (bearer attach only; refresh/retry/typed errors are REQ-425's). All HTTP in this and later requirements goes through it. 8. docs/mobile/requirements.md MOB-2's first acceptance bullet and docs/mobile/architecture.md §3 row 1 list the five-key tenant-config shape; append a dated note to each that REQ-418 added client_id as a sixth key and that the app consumes it (keep the original text).
LIVE LOGIN caveat: completing a real Keycloak login requires typing credentials into a Custom Tab, which `flutter test` cannot drive. Acceptance is therefore split: the full sequence is proven by widget /unit tests with a fake AppAuth adapter and a fake HTTP layer; a live emulator run proves the app reaches Keycloak's login page for two different slugs; the interactive credential entry is DEFERRED to UAT-RUNNER with that reason recorded.

task.description: Produce the design artefact(s) for REQ-421 (MOB-2 tenant bootstrap / OIDC auth flow) at lib/letflow/design/req421-mobile-tenant-bootstrap.md, per code-designer.md and WF-02 Step 1's procedure. Read the requirement text above in full plus every artifacts_in path (especially the two existing mobile design docs, REQ-418/419, for established naming conventions -- e.g. how tenant-config's response shape and the secure-storage key scheme are already named -- and the two backend router files for the exact endpoint response shapes this design consumes). Design every module this requirement's SEQUENCE describes: (1) deep-link/slug parsing (a pure function taking a URL and the build-time platform host, returning slug-or-null; the manual-entry path; the AndroidManifest intent-filter shape, host pattern built from a build-time platform-host define, autoVerify state and the assetlinks.json DEFERRED note); (2) a tenant-config client function (GET .../api/mobile/tenant-config?slug=, explicitly no Authorization header, response type covering all six keys including REQ-418's client_id); (3) the OIDC flow via flutter_appauth's authorizeAndExchangeCode -- exact issuer/clientId/redirectUrl/PKCE parameters, sourced from the tenant-config response, never a compiled constant; (4) the ONE token-store class in lib/auth/, its interface (store/read/delete, keyed by realm_url/tenant), and state plainly that REQ-421 must not introduce any second storage path (REQ-422 will harden this same class -- do not design REQ-422's own guards here, just leave the seam); (5) the post-auth bootstrap sequence -- GET /me/memberships and /me/modules, the tenant-not-found rule (first membership entry's tenant_slug must equal the entered slug, else show tenant-not-found and delete tokens -- even if a later entry matches), the CANDIDATE 403-on-memberships fallback path, and the installed_modules-driven route table (a module absent from installed_modules has no route); (6) the four dedicated error screens (tenant-not-found, network-unavailable, OIDC-failure, secure-storage-unavailable) -- widget/screen signatures and what triggers each; (7) lib/api/api_client.dart as the single Dio-construction site (bearer-attach only in this requirement); (8) the exact dated-note text to append to docs/mobile/requirements.md MOB-2's first acceptance bullet and docs/mobile/architecture.md §3 row 1 (keep original text, additive only). State every function's @spec-style signature, error-tuple shapes, and data-class field lists. No implementation code bodies -- signatures and type shapes only. List cross-module dependencies (flutter_appauth, flutter_secure_storage, dio, go_router or whatever routing package REQ-419 already established -- check, don't guess). Flag open questions explicitly rather than silently resolving them (e.g. exact platform-host build-time define name if not already fixed by REQ-418/419 -- check those artefacts before flagging as open).
acceptance_criteria: a test asserts the tenant-config request carries no Authorization header, and asserts the authorization request built for a slug uses issuer == that response's realm_url, clientId == that response's client_id, redirectUrl 'com.bizdala.letflow:/oauth2redirect' and a PKCE S256 challenge

a test drives the whole sequence for two distinct slugs whose fake tenant-config responses carry different realm_url values in ONE app instance with no rebuild, and asserts each ends with tokens stored under its own tenant key and that tenant B's API calls never carry tenant A's access token (MOB-1's two-tenant criterion)

a test asserts no tenant content route is reachable before /me/memberships and /me/modules have both resolved, and that a module absent from installed_modules has no route (navigating to its path shows the not-found screen)

a test asserts a login whose /me/memberships FIRST entry has a tenant_slug different from the entered slug shows the tenant-not-found screen and leaves no token in the secure store -- including a case where a later entry does match the entered slug; and a test asserts a 403 from /me/memberships (CANDIDATE) proceeds to /me/modules instead of failing

a unit test asserts the deep-link parser extracts slug 'acme' from https://acme.<configured platform host>/any/path and rejects a URL on any other host (returning no slug rather than guessing); the AndroidManifest intent filter is quoted showing a host pattern built from the build-time platform host, and the report records App Link verification (assetlinks.json) as DEFERRED with its reason
docs/mobile/requirements.md MOB-2 and docs/mobile/architecture.md §3 each carry the dated client_id note, with the original five-key text still present (git diff shows additions only there)

four widget tests each force one failure -- tenant-not-found (per the post-login membership rule), SocketException, AppAuth error, secure-storage exception -- and assert the corresponding dedicated screen (by key) is shown, not a generic error or a crash
`git grep -n 'Dio(' -- apps/mobile/lib` returns exactly one hit, in lib/api/api_client.dart, quoted
every acceptance criterion above maps to a concrete design element with no TBD/deferral language, and no implementation code bodies are present in the design doc
